faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Williamsburg?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing and cleanup the job needs. Our crew inspects first, shows you the entry points we found in Williamsburg, and gives you a quote after inspection before any removal or sealing work begins — no prices promised over the phone.

faqs.q: When can bats be removed from a Williamsburg attic?
faqs.a: Bats in Virginia are handled by exclusion only — one-way exits fitted and every other opening sealed so the colony leaves on its own. Under our permit conditions the maternity season runs May 1 through August 15, and bats may not be excluded or removed then unless no young are present or there is a threat to human health or safety, so we inspect any time but schedule most Williamsburg exclusions outside that window. Since January 1, 2025, bat work also requires a CNAP holder with DWR-recognized bat training, which is how our crew works.

Williamsburg.wildlife_intro:
Williamsburg is a small historic city surrounded by James City and York counties, with carefully kept older housing in Williamsburg. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: colonial Williamsburg's historic area, William & Mary campus, York River country nearby. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Williamsburg — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
